mechanisms.problemSolved: A scroll-scrubbed multi-scene film needs a single flat timeline (scroll position -> which clip, and how far into it) built from a designer's per-section config, without hand-computing pixel ranges.
mechanisms.mechanism: Builds a flat SEGMENTS array by walking SECTIONS and interleaving a dive segment per section with an optional conn segment between consecutive sections (skipped when connectors[i] is falsy). Each segment carries a scroll-width weight; layout() turns weights into cumulative pixel start/end offsets.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Decouples 'what media exists and in what order' (editable config) from 'how much scroll height that requires' (computed) and 'what is currently active' (derived per scroll tick).
requiredContext: a config object with an ordered sections array and an optional connectors array
mechanisms.outputImpact: The load-bearing data structure the entire engine reads from.
failureModes: No validation that connectors.length === sections.length - 1; a mismatch silently misaligns connectors.
mechanisms.testMethod: No automated test in repo; correctness implied by rest of engine working.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: Reuse this shape for any SiteSmith scroll-scrubbed hero: ordered scene array with optional connector slots, flattened to a weighted timeline at layout time, independent of clip source.

mechanisms.problemSolved: Setting video.currentTime from scroll silently fails on hosts without HTTP byte-range support: seekable pins to [0,0] and every seek clamps to frame 0.
mechanisms.mechanism: loadClip() fetches each clip via fetch().then(blob) and plays it from URL.createObjectURL(blob) instead of a direct network src.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Sidesteps the root cause (server range support) entirely by scrubbing an in-memory object; this is why all-intra encoding is unnecessary.
requiredContext: clip URL fetchable same-origin or CORS-permitting
mechanisms.outputImpact: Without this the entire premise (scroll-scrubbed video) breaks on many static hosts.
failureModes: Loads whole clip into memory before scrubbable — fine for short clips, wouldn't scale to long-form video.
Silent catch on fetch failure permanently skips that clip for the session.
mechanisms.testMethod: Asserted only; well-known browser behavior, independently verifiable.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: Standard technique for any SiteSmith build scrubbing video by scroll position: fetch-to-blob before scrubbing, assume static-host byte-range gaps by default.

mechanisms.problemSolved: Even frame-matched clip boundaries need a visual handoff rather than an instantaneous cut between video elements.
mechanisms.mechanism: read() computes pixel distance to each segment's start/end and maps it through a smoothstep to set opacity/z-index, cross-dissolving over a configurable crossfade band around each seam.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: A short dissolve masks small residual mismatch at a seam without requiring perfect asset continuity; complements frame-matching rather than replacing it.
mechanisms.outputImpact: Directly determines whether transitions look connected or cut.
failureModes: Content-agnostic — will mask a genuinely mismatched pair of clips just as readily as a well-matched one.
mechanisms.testMethod: None automated; verified by eye per the source's own QA step.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: Generic rule for SiteSmith: any two adjacent scroll-bound media segments cross-dissolve over N vh at their shared boundary, regardless of media source.

mechanisms.problemSolved: A linear scroll-to-time mapping gives no way to make a scene's best/most narratively important frame coincide with the moment its copy peaks.
mechanisms.mechanism: lingerEase(x, L) is a monotone cubic remap that flattens the middle of a segment's range and steepens the edges as L rises, while preserving f(0)=0 and f(1)=1 exactly.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: A single per-section parameter changes pacing without touching the clip or breaking the seam guarantee.
requiredContext: local progress x within a segment (0..1)
mechanisms.outputImpact: Pacing/craft refinement, not a correctness fix.
failureModes: L close to 1 with a short scroll distance can feel stuck; source recommends L<=0.6 but doesn't enforce it.
mechanisms.testMethod: None automated.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: Reusable as-is: boundary-preserving cubic ease with a single linger parameter per scroll-bound section.

mechanisms.problemSolved: Scroll-scrubbed video has several distinct phone failure modes: fast-flick seek pileup, iOS blank-muted-video quirk, URL-bar resize scroll jump, heavier decode budget.
mechanisms.mechanism: Four bundled fixes behind one isMobile() check: seek-coalescing (skip re-queuing currentTime while still seeking), iOS priming (muted play/pause on first touch, wait for 'seeked' not just 'loadedmetadata'), resize-gating (ignore height-only resize on touch), coarser mobile seek epsilon.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Each fix targets one concrete, named bug, independently testable and removable, matched to the source's own Gotchas list.
requiredContext: coarse-pointer/viewport-width check at mount plus live width tracking
mechanisms.outputImpact: High for mobile visitors — without this the same engine reliably breaks on iOS Safari and stutters on mid-range Android.
failureModes: coarse pointer check captured once at mount, never re-evaluated (acknowledged intentional).
mechanisms.testMethod: None automated; source recommends manual CPU-throttled and real-device iOS testing.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: Adopt all four as a standard checklist for any SiteSmith scroll-video build; none depend on how the video was produced.

mechanisms.problemSolved: prefers-reduced-motion should stop clip loading entirely, not just disable visible animation while still fetching/decoding video.
mechanisms.mechanism: reduce is read once at mount; loadClip() short-circuits immediately if true, leaving only stills that cross-dissolve via the same opacity math used for seams.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Full degrade at the fetch layer, not a cosmetic override — no wasted bandwidth/decode, reuses existing code paths for the fallback.
mechanisms.outputImpact: Satisfies accessibility requirement; the same path is the only fully-graceful route when video assets are entirely unavailable.
failureModes: Only triggers on OS-level preference; no separate opt-in for bandwidth/low-end-device reasons.
mechanisms.testMethod: None automated; testable by toggling the OS setting.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: Gate any generated/heavy media fetch behind the same check used to gate its motion, so accessibility and 'no backend available' share one code path.

mechanisms.problemSolved: A component injecting default CSS custom properties needs a host page's own theme rules to win without predicting every selector or using !important.
mechanisms.mechanism: The engine's injected stylesheet is wrapped in @layer sw; unlayered page CSS always outranks @layer-wrapped CSS regardless of specificity or order.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Native platform feature doing what a specificity hack would otherwise require, order-independent.
requiredContext: browser support for CSS @layer, broadly available
mechanisms.outputImpact: Removes an entire class of theming bugs for near-zero cost.
failureModes: No fallback noted for browsers without @layer support.
mechanisms.testMethod: None automated; a verifiable CSS-cascade fact.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: Wrap any SiteSmith-authored component's default CSS custom properties in @layer, leave host page theme rules unlayered.

mechanisms.problemSolved: Naive assumptions about scrub smoothness (all-intra encoding, quality downscaling) are backwards; the real levers are seekability and keyframe distance.
mechanisms.mechanism: Native resolution, crf ~20, small GOP (-g 8, not all-intra), stripped audio, +faststart, light unsharp; a tighter mobile profile (-g 4, 720p, crf 23) trades keyframes for cheaper phone-decoder seeks.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Ties every setting to a stated cause rather than folklore, with two calibrated presets instead of one compromise.
mechanisms.outputImpact: Determines whether scroll-scrubbed video feels smooth or stutters/bloats.
failureModes: Tuned for short (5-10s) clips; not claimed to hold for longer-form video.
mechanisms.testMethod: None automated in-repo; asserted from experience, not measured in this codebase.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: Carry as reference documentation for any SiteSmith scroll-video build regardless of asset source.

mechanisms.problemSolved: Heavy reference material inlined into a main procedure file bloats context on every invocation even for steps a build never reaches.
mechanisms.mechanism: SKILL.md is the only always-loaded file; it names each reference file by relative path at the exact step it's needed, none pre-loaded speculatively.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Matches the general skill-authoring principle of separating procedure from heavy reference data.
requiredContext: an agent runtime that can read a named file mid-procedure
mechanisms.outputImpact: Keeps always-loaded cost to SKILL.md alone rather than the full combined reference total, though SKILL.md itself is still large (see CONTEXT-STRATEGY.md).
failureModes: SKILL.md still inlines ~150 lines of volatile vendor pricing/schema tables that belong in a deferred reference file instead.
mechanisms.testMethod: Verified directly by reading SKILL.md and confirming reference files are named only at point of use.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: Keep the pattern but apply more strictly: move vendor-pricing/model-capability tables out of the main procedure file into a reference file.

mechanisms.problemSolved: A fabricated multiple-choice list of subjects at intake biases the user and reads as the assistant deciding their business for them.
mechanisms.mechanism: Instructs asking the subject as an open plain-prose question, reserving structured multiple-choice for genuinely enumerable, lower-stakes choices later, always with an 'Other' escape hatch.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: A reasoning/prompting instruction about when structured choice helps versus constrains — the same category as the frontend-design skill's winning mechanisms.
mechanisms.outputImpact: Affects the quality of the first interaction in a build; a biased intake question propagates downstream.
failureModes: No mechanism verifies the model actually asked openly rather than defaulting to a menu under time pressure.
mechanisms.testMethod: Asserted only.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: Extract the general rule for SiteSmith's own interview step: ask identity-defining questions as open prose, reserve structured choice for genuinely enumerable, lower-stakes decisions with an explicit 'describe your own' option.

mechanisms.problemSolved: Silently substituting an incompatible tool/model for a user's stated preference produces a broken result without explanation.
mechanisms.mechanism: States the selection rule as a hard capability check, directing that an out-of-roster request be declined with a one-line reason rather than silently substituted.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Fail-loud-with-reason beats silent substitution or silent failure.
requiredContext: a way to introspect the chosen tool's actual capability contract before depending on it
mechanisms.outputImpact: Prevents a specific silent-failure class, low frequency but meaningful when triggered.
failureModes: Entirely dependent on a capability-introspection command existing for the tool in question.
mechanisms.testMethod: Asserted only; no automated check in-repo.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: General engineering discipline, not a discrete feature: verify a requested library/API/font actually supports the plan before committing, say so if not. Low priority to formalize.

mechanisms.problemSolved: Metered, real-money generation needs informed user consent on cost before rendering, since mid-run failure is recoverable but ugly.
mechanisms.mechanism: Presents render tiers with a cost table, computes an estimated total from actual scene count/mobile choice, calibrates against live balance, requires explicit go-ahead.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: State the number, get consent, then act — sound wherever an action has irreversible metered cost.
requiredContext: a billed backend with an inspectable balance/pricing API
mechanisms.outputImpact: High stakes when applicable, zero relevance without a metered backend.
failureModes: No analogue at all when there is no paid, metered generation step in the build.
conflicts: Conflicts with SiteSmith's current scope: no metered paid-generation backend exists to protect against.
mechanisms.testMethod: Asserted only.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: No coherent role in SiteSmith today. Revisit only if a paid generation backend is wired in as a build-time dependency.

mechanisms.problemSolved: Two independently-generated video clips meant to connect won't visually match because every generation renders slightly differently.
mechanisms.mechanism: Requires a connector's conditioning images be the ACTUAL last/first frame extracted from already-rendered neighbouring clips, never the original source still, so seams are frame-identical by construction.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: A generalizable idea (condition on your own actual prior output, not the original input, to prevent drift across a generative chain) but only actionable with a generative backend that supports image conditioning.
requiredContext: a video-generation backend accepting image conditioning on both ends of a clip
mechanisms.outputImpact: The rule the source calls out as the difference between a connected world and a visibly cut one — entirely inside the paid-pipeline half.
failureModes: Zero applicability without a generative video backend — there is no 'next frame' to extract when clips aren't generated in a chain.
conflicts: SiteSmith has no generative video backend, so there is no chain to keep frame-identical.
mechanisms.testMethod: Manual screenshot diffing; no automated frame-comparison tool ships in the repo.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: Not applicable to SiteSmith today. The abstract idea (condition on actual own output, not original input) is worth remembering but has no concrete SiteSmith use case.

mechanisms.problemSolved: Frames 'cohesion' as fixing art direction to a small enumerated set (clay diorama/papercraft/glossy toy/claymation/neon-night) and camera behavior to a 3-way roster, reused verbatim across a build.
mechanisms.mechanism: A shared style preamble composed once at intake is reused byte-for-byte in every scene prompt; camera behavior is selected once from a fixed roster and applied uniformly.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Genuinely produces per-build cohesion, but the same mechanism shape (small fixed menu of looks reused verbatim) is what this project's own three-site convergence test flagged as a liability, just scoped to one genre instead of SiteSmith's whole output.
requiredContext: the shared style preamble and chosen camera architecture, held fixed for the whole build
mechanisms.outputImpact: High within a build; a house-style risk if generalized as SiteSmith's default answer to scroll storytelling.
failureModes: Every build necessarily looks like a member of the same small family by design — no mechanism for the model to invent a genuinely novel treatment per subject.
Two unrelated businesses choosing the same defaults converge on similar sites for structural reasons, not coincidence.
conflicts: Directly in tension with the measured fact that a fixed-look mechanism is a liability even when each output is individually good.
mechanisms.testMethod: Not tested for cross-build convergence in the source.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: Do not adopt the fixed style-roster shape. If a scroll-cinematic capability is ever offered, treat art direction/camera behavior as brief-driven creative decisions reasoned per project, not a preset menu.

mechanisms.problemSolved: Removing a flat background from a still while preserving interior regions that happen to match the background colour.
mechanisms.mechanism: Samples corner pixels as background colour, flood-fills from the image border inward within an RGB-distance tolerance, so only border-connected pixels are knocked out; blurs the alpha mask edge.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Border-connectivity is correct for this pipeline's exact 'floating island on solid background' framing — a small, correctly-scoped algorithm, not a general background remover.
mechanisms.outputImpact: Cosmetic-only, explicitly optional in the source itself.
failureModes: Tolerance-based matching can eat into subject pixels near the background colour.
Assumes a genuinely flat corner-sampled background; fails silently on gradient/textured backgrounds.
mechanisms.testMethod: None automated; visual inspection only.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: No current SiteSmith use case — serves the AI-diorama pipeline's own visual convention, which SiteSmith isn't adopting. Revisit only if a specific feature needs solid-background cutout.

perSourceVerdict.oneLineVerdict: A well-engineered, portable scroll-scrub front-end engine bolted onto a single-vendor paid video-generation pipeline and a fixed-aesthetic creative template — take the engine, leave the rest.
perSourceVerdict.bestThingToSteal: scrub-engine.js in full: the segment/scene data model, blob-based scrubbing (fixes the byte-range-host freeze bug at the root), and the four-part mobile-hardening bundle (seek-coalescing, iOS priming, resize-gating, coarser mobile epsilon) — all zero-dependency and completely decoupled from how the clips were produced.
perSourceVerdict.mostDangerousThingToCopy: The shared style-preamble + fixed 3-way camera-architecture roster that gives one build its cohesion — the same small-fixed-menu-of-looks shape our own three-site convergence test measured as a liability, just scoped to one genre instead of SiteSmith's whole output.

autopsy.notApplicable: The entire paid video-generation pipeline is not applicable to SiteSmith: Steps 0 (Bootstrap CLI checks), 2 (Higgsfield/Codex still generation), 4 (video-model roster, Monid backend wiring, camera-grammar prompt library), and 5 (frame-identical seam chaining between generated clips) all require a Monid or Higgsfield account and real metered spend that SiteSmith has no equivalent for. The budget/cost-negotiation portion of Step 1 (render-tier tables, credit estimates, live-balance calibration) is likewise inert without a metered backend to protect spend against. The fixed aesthetic mechanism (one style preamble reused verbatim, one camera architecture applied uniformly per build) is explicitly rejected rather than merely inapplicable — it conflicts with this project's own measured house-style-convergence finding. knockout.py's border-flood-fill background removal is a correctly-scoped but narrow utility that exists only to serve this pipeline's own 'floating diorama on solid background' visual convention; SiteSmith has no current feature that needs standalone image-cutout, so it is not applicable now (though the algorithm, if a real need arises later, is the right one to reach for over a naive global colour-key). Vendor-specific gotchas (NSFW filter false positives, Monid's sfs file-relay quirks, per-model flag differences, endpoint qualification probes) are all bound to the rejected pipeline half and carry no transferable technique beyond the general 'verify capability before depending on it' principle already captured separately.

challenge.overallVerdict: 6 of 9 claims confirmed against the actual source; 3 refuted — one for miscited/mismatched line ranges (part of the mechanism lives outside the cited lines, and the extra CSS citation doesn't support the claim), one for treating the boilerplate closing References list as proof of a distinctive just-in-time-loading mechanism (a generic skill-authoring pattern, not distinctive to scroll-world), and the remaining claim's core mechanism was confirmed but one embedded comparative assertion in its rationale could not be verified.

challenges.claim: SEGMENTS built by walking SECTIONS, interleaving optional conn segments, weights turned into cumulative offsets by layout()
challenges.reason: Opened scrub-engine.js:86-101: SEGMENTS.push(dive) at 91, conditional CONNECTORS[i] push at 96-100, exactly as described. layout()'s cumulative-offset math (s.start=off*vh; off+=s.w; s.end=off*vh) is real but lives at lines 182-191, outside the cited 86-101 range — the claim folds in behavior from an uncited function. Core interleaving mechanism itself is verified.

challenges.claim: loadClip() fetches each clip as a Blob and plays it via URL.createObjectURL instead of a direct network src, to sidestep missing byte-range support
challenges.reason: Opened scrub-engine.js:198-220: fetch(url).then(blob).then(v.src = URL.createObjectURL(blob)) at lines 205-211, matching exactly. SKILL.md:528-533 states the byte-range rationale ('fetch each clip as a Blob... you do not need all-intra video') consistent with the claim.

challenges.claim: read() computes pixel distance to segment start/end, maps through smoothstep to opacity/z-index for seam crossfade
challenges.reason: Opened scrub-engine.js:222-242: outside = s.start-y or y-s.end (line 234), op = smooth(1-outside/fade) (line 235, smooth() is the classic x*x*(3-2x) smoothstep defined at line 174), applied to s.el.style.opacity and zIndex (236-237). Matches claim exactly.

challenges.claim: lingerEase(x,L) is a monotone cubic remap flattening the segment middle and steepening edges as L rises, with f(0)=0 and f(1)=1 exactly
challenges.reason: Opened scrub-engine.js:175-178: lingerEase = (1-L)*x + L*(4c^3+0.5) with c=x-0.5. Hand-verified f(0): c=-0.5, 4c^3=-0.5, +0.5=0, term=0 -> result 0. f(1): c=0.5, 4c^3=0.5,+0.5=1, result 1. Usage at line 232 (s.target = s.linger ? lingerEase(local, s.linger) : local) matches.

challenges.claim: Four bundled mobile fixes (seek-coalescing, iOS priming incl. waiting for 'seeked' not just 'loadedmetadata', resize-gating, coarser mobile epsilon) behind isMobile(), matched to the Gotchas list
challenges.reason: 3 of 4 sub-parts check out inside the cited ranges: seek-coalescing at line 281 (if s.video.seeking continue), resize-gating at 317-320, coarser epsilon at line 274 — all within 273-323. But the 'wait for seeked not just loadedmetadata' detail actually lives in loadClip() at line 216, outside the cited 66-73,273-323 ranges entirely. The additional CSS citation (413-435) is generic mobile layout media queries (nav hiding, copy anchoring, route dot hit-area) and contains none of the four described JS fixes — it doesn't support the claim at all. The claim merges code from an uncited location and an unrelated CSS block into one citation.
challenges.evidencePath: skills/scroll-world/references/scrub-engine.js:66-73,216,273-323; CSS 413-435 (does not contain the described fixes)

challenges.claim: reduce read once at mount; loadClip() short-circuits if true; only stills cross-dissolve via the same opacity math used for seams
challenges.reason: Opened scrub-engine.js:67 (reduce captured once at mount) and 199-201 (loadClip returns immediately if reduce is true). read()'s opacity/crossfade math at 233-236 runs unconditionally for every segment regardless of reduce, so stills do cross-dissolve via the same code path. CSS line 436 is a minor secondary detail (hides hint-arrow animation/particles), not central to the claim but not contradicting it either.

challenges.claim: Injected stylesheet wrapped in @layer sw so unlayered page CSS always outranks it regardless of specificity/order
challenges.reason: Opened scrub-engine.js:438-444: style.textContent = '@layer sw {\n' + css + '\n}' at line 442, with an explicit comment at 438-440 stating the intent. This matches real CSS cascade-layer semantics (unlayered rules beat layered ones regardless of specificity/order).

challenges.claim: Native resolution, crf~20, small GOP (-g 8, not all-intra), stripped audio, +faststart, light unsharp; tighter mobile profile -g 4, 720p, crf 23
challenges.reason: Opened SKILL.md:534-543 and pipeline.md:119-132: enc() uses crf 20, -g 8 -keyint_min 8, -an, +faststart, unsharp=5:5:0.8:5:5:0.0 exactly. Mobile encm() at pipeline.md:149-156 uses scale to 720, crf 23, -g 4 -keyint_min 4, matching the claim precisely, including the stated rationale (phone seek cost scales with frames-from-keyframe).

challenges.claim: SKILL.md is the only always-loaded file; it names each reference file by relative path at the exact step it's needed, none pre-loaded speculatively
challenges.reason: The cited lines 752-762 are just the final '## References' summary list at the end of SKILL.md — a bare enumeration of the reference files with one-line descriptions, not evidence of just-in-time referencing throughout the steps. The claim's own whyItWorks concedes this 'matches the general skill-authoring principle' — i.e. this is standard Claude-skill structure (SKILL.md as sole entry point, references loaded on demand), not a distinctive mechanism of scroll-world. Treated as a platitude dressed up as a mechanism; the citation doesn't show what's actually being claimed (loading discipline at each step) — that would require citing the scattered inline 'See references/X' pointers throughout Steps 1-8, not the closing list.

challenges.claim: Instructs asking the subject via open plain-prose question, reserving structured multiple-choice for enumerable lower-stakes choices, always with an 'Other' escape hatch
challenges.reason: Opened SKILL.md:80-93: verified verbatim — 'ask it as an open question in plain prose, never a fabricated multiple-choice... Reserve structured multiple-choice... for the genuinely enumerable, lower-stakes choices below — art direction, camera style, and brand-kit approach — and even there, signal they can go their own way ("Other")'. This is a specific, concrete instruction, not a vague platitude. Caveat: the whyItWorks claim that this is 'the same category as the frontend-design skill's winning mechanisms' is an unverifiable comparison to a file not provided in evidence — that specific comparative assertion could not be checked, though it does not change the underlying mechanism's authenticity.

mechanisms.problemSolved: Agent starts writing a spec/plan on an underspecified request and locks in a wrong interpretation before the user can correct it.
mechanisms.mechanism: Cap clarifying questions at 3-5, ask only where the prompt is ambiguous or missing essential context, present lettered options so the user answers in one line, and forbid starting implementation before questions are answered.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: A thinking aid, not a lookup table: changes what the model asks itself before acting. Independently corroborated by grill-for-unknowns' material/grounded/answerable bar (SKILL.md:92-118) — two unrelated sources converging on 'ask fewer, sharper questions' is stronger signal than either alone.
mechanisms.outputImpact: Prevents building the wrong thing; does not by itself prevent generic-looking output.
failureModes: Turns into an exhaustive questionnaire if the cap/ambiguity guard is dropped
Lettered options can railroad the user if not genuinely representative
conflicts: Magnus's house rule 'Beslut, spørg ikke' — resolve by keeping the cap very small and only asking when it changes scope/architecture
mechanisms.testMethod: Run the same ambiguous brief twice; confirm it asks <=5 questions once, then doesn't re-ask already-answered material.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: Pre-build question gate: max 2-3 lettered questions, asked only when the brief is silent on something that changes layout/scope/brand feel.

mechanisms.problemSolved: Scope creep and no shared definition of done for a build.
mechanisms.mechanism: Of 9 mandated PRD sections, Non-Goals (Out of Scope) and Success Metrics carry real weight for scope control and a concrete definition of done.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Cheap, model-facing constraint rather than a rendering rule (Fact 1). Directly counters house-style convergence if 'do not converge on the same layout as the last brief' is stated as a non-goal.
requiredContext: prior similar builds to name as an explicit non-goal reference
mechanisms.outputImpact: Reduces scope drift and gives a checkable definition of done; does not itself diversify visual output.
failureModes: Non-goals left as boilerplate 'N/A'
Success metrics stated only in engineering terms, missing the visual-sameness failure mode
conflicts: The full 9-section PRD template this is extracted from
mechanisms.testMethod: Check a completed brief for an explicit Non-Goals line and Success Metrics line; confirm the build was checked against both.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: Two required lines in brief-intake: 'will not look like <named prior site>' and 'done means <concrete criterion>'.

mechanisms.problemSolved: A human junior developer misreading a spec.
mechanisms.mechanism: Both files instruct writing for a 'junior developer': explicit, unambiguous, jargon-free.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Rejected: the audience for SiteSmith is always a capable model reading a compact instruction, not a junior human.
